newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Sanjiu aims to offer one billion H shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Sanjiu aims to offer one billion H shares.

text.p: China's Sanjiu Pharmaceutical Co Ltd plans to offer between 900 million and one billion H shares and list them on the Hong Kong stock exchange in the second quarter of 1997, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The pricing of the offer has not been fixed, and an underwriter has yet to be chosen for the issue, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The Shenzhen-based drug maker is among 38 domestic firms newly selected by China's Securities Commission of the State Council, or the cabinet, for listing on overseas stock markets.

The firm, part of the Sanjiu Group conglomerate under the General Logistics Department of the People's Liberation Army, would use the proceeds to produce and market new pharmaceutical products if the issue is successful, the official said.
Sanjiu Pharmaceutical expects its net profits next year to roughly equal 1996's level of 300 million yuan against 280 million yuan recorded in 1995, he said.
Sanjiu Pharmaceutical's total share capital will not be released until the ongoing restructuring of its assets is completed, he said.
